question: When was she hit?
claim: 1250 Item
source: Haynsworth action report, p. 3 (9 Apr 1945)
note: "striking at 1250 Item". The ship's own report, three days after

question: When was she hit?
claim: Fires under control about 1300
source: Haynsworth war diary, p. 4
note: Typed "By13??" with an overstrike. Favours a hit before 1300

question: When was she hit?
source: COMDESRON 62 war diary, p. 8
note: The squadron commander's diary

question: When was she hit?
claim: 1321 (report received)
source: South Dakota war diary, 6 Apr
note: "reported having received a bomb hit". Her radio was wrecked, so the report was late: this is when the news arrived, not when it happened

question: What hit her?
claim: A Judy (Suisei)
source: Action report p. 3; war diary p. 3
note: The ship called it a Judy throughout

question: What hit her?
claim: The engine was a two-row radial
source: Ship's photo No. 26 (4228-45), in Irons, Phalanx
note: Rules out a Suisei Model 11 or 12 (inline Atsuta). Fits a Model 33, and also a Zeke 52

question: What hit her?
claim: The machine gun was a 7.7 mm Type 97
source: Ship's photo No. 27 (4824-45), in Irons, Phalanx
note: The Suisei and the Zeke 52 both carried Type 97s in the cowling. Doesn't separate them

question: What hit her?
claim: "Blew his exterior bomb loose"
source: XO Lothrop's letters, in Irons, Phalanx
note: An external bomb sits better with a Zeke, whose bomb hung under the fuselage. Lothrop was in CIC

question: What hit her?
claim: Dived, pulled out, headed away, then turned back
source: Action report, p. 3
note: The pattern of a dive-bomber whose attack failed, not a Zeke on a crash run. Leans Judy

question: What hit her?
claim: The task group mixed up Judys and Zekes within the hour
source: Bunker Hill diary p. 8; Astoria pp. 64-66
note: Bunker Hill called the 1302 Zeke a Judy; Astoria called the 1226 Judy a Zeke. One ship's identification under fire is weak evidence

question: Who flew it?
claim: One of the 210th Air Group's seven
source: Irons, Phalanx (uncited); 210th action report, form pp. 9, 17, 23
note: Seven Suisei sent southeast of Tokunoshima, presumed to have dived in 1200-1300. Time, place and type agree. No Japanese record names a ship

question: Who flew it?
claim: One of the other 12 Suisei of Fifth Air Fleet
source: Fifth Air Fleet operations record, pp. 11-13
note: 23 Suisei went at TF 58 between 1015 and 1310; the 210th supplied 11. The 252nd's four have no launch time. Any that left after about 1120 couldn't have reached her by 1250

question: Who flew it?
claim: A bomb-carrying Zero
source: Fifth Air Fleet record; Bennington, Hancock and Cabot reports
note: 30 bomb-carrying Zeros went with the Suisei. They reached TF 58 at the same minutes: Bennington 1253, Hancock 1302, Cabot 1302

question: How many died?
claim: 7 killed outright
source: War diary p. 4; action report p. 5; COMDESRON 62 p. 8
note: The seven named on the Report of Casualties, items 1-7

question: How many died?
claim: 12 in all
source: Action report, p. 5
note: "five additional deaths" aboard South Dakota by 9 April. Irons agrees, and names four of the five; the fifth isn't found yet

question: How many were wounded?
source: War diary (11 + 14); action report (27); COMDESRON 62 (14); Irons, Phalanx (19)
note: Counts made on different days and before or after the deaths aboard South Dakota

question: Where did the bomb go?
claim: "Released or ... knocked off in the turn", 1,000 yards abeam
source: Action report, p. 3
note: The ship wasn't sure which

question: Where did the bomb go?
claim: "One of our bursts blew his exterior bomb loose"
source: Lothrop, in Irons, Phalanx

question: Where did the bomb go?
claim: "I did see the Japanese plane drop its bomb as it flew away from us"
source: Weldon Powell (starboard quad 40 mm director), in Irons, Phalanx

question: How many airmen died aboard?
claim: One Japanese airman's body was found aboard
source: Irons, Phalanx, from the crew
note: Left alone for some time for fear it was booby-trapped. The action report and diary don't mention it

question: How many airmen died aboard?
claim: Every Suisei that day carried two men
source: 210th crew list, form p. 23
note: So a Judy should leave two. The second could have gone over the side with the wreckage, which was jettisoned. A Zero would leave one

question: Where were the dead buried?
claim: At sea, 7 April 1945, 1816
source: Irons, Phalanx, from crew diaries
note: Not in the war diary or action report
